subject: Console request: fast-inspect for per-route cost & tail-latency (Quasar Labs spike)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Console request: fast-inspect for per-route cost & tail-latency (Quasar Labs spike)

Team —

Quasar Labs flagged a sudden cost and tail-latency spike tied to their main /generate-chat route yesterday afternoon. They’re seeing a 4–6x token-cost bump on a subset of calls and occasional 95th/99th latency spikes that align with heavy prompt prefixes.

They asked for a quick way for us to answer:
- Which routes and caller tokens contributed most to the cost spike (top N callers, per-route token breakdown).
- Whether the model variant, batch size, or quantization profile changed during the window.
- Fast traces that show model latency by token and the top-cost tokens so we can correlate to prompt patterns.

Request: build a ‘fast-inspect’ UX in Console that gives a lightweight, queryable slice (1–12 hour window) for any route: top callers, token-cost histogram, model-variant, batch-size, and an attached sample trace. This needs to be actionable for support/SEs to triage in <15min.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Per-route top-10 caller list with token-count + cost estimate
- Token-level latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) for the selected window
- Surface model-variant and batch-size in the UI and link to traces
- Exportable CSV and a small sample trace (JSON) for root-cause analysis

Timeline: Quasar is sensitive; they want an experiment in 3 sprints. Please call out any infra/data constraints and a minimal mitigations plan to ship a narrow MVP. I’ve attached their spike summary and one sample trace.

Avery
Avery Johnson
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console request: fast-inspect for per-route cost & tail-latency (Quasar Labs spike)

Thanks for the note — quick thoughts and a few clarifying questions.

Feasibility notes:
- We can implement a lightweight per-request fingerprinting index (route + caller id + model-variant + batch-size + cost estimate) that supports fast top-N queries, but it requires an additional write path at the inference edge (small payload per request). Storage for 30 days of 1% sampled write will be ~30–60 GB depending on cardinality.
- Token-level latency histograms are more expensive. We should sample full token traces (1–5% of requests) and pre-aggregate short-window histograms for the rest.

Questions:
1) Do we need full retention for all customers, or can we start with Quasar-only canary retention?
2) Is the 15min triage SLA strict, or is a 30min response acceptable for MVP?

Proposed approach for MVP (spike -> MVP -> canary):
- Spike (3 days): instrument sampling + run storage estimate, validate cost numbers (I’ll attach a rough cost sheet).
- MVP (2 sprints): implement index + per-route UI + sampled token traces + CSV export.
- Canary (1 sprint): enable for Quasar (and a few internal tenants) and iterate on UX.

I’ll spin up a spike ticket and attach a rough storage/cost estimate. If we can limit retention to 7 days for canary, storage/cost jumps are manageable.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Software Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Console request: fast-inspect for per-route cost & tail-latency (Quasar Labs spike)

Adding customer context — Quasar is running a production pilot and this spike directly impacts their monthly commit. They’ve asked SEs for an explanation and hinted at pausing some usage if costs remain opaque.

I spoke to Sam (CC’d) and they’re ok with a Quasar-only canary if it means faster delivery. They can also enable additional request logging on their side for the 72-hour window we need.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/QL-4721 — moving this to high priority on the renewal track. If we can offer a temporary mitigation (route-level soft cap or model fallback) that’s likely to buy time and reduce churn risk.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Apr 2029 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console request: fast-inspect for per-route cost & tail-latency (Quasar Labs spike)

Operational mitigation options we can do immediately:
- Add a temporary per-route token cap (soft throttle) at the edge to limit runaway prompts — can be enabled in ~6 hours and rolled back.
- Add automatic fallback to a smaller model variant for the route on cost-surge detection — needs a coordinated rollout but possible in ~1 business day for limited traffic.

For the fast-inspect data work: we need a small infra spike to validate write latency impact. If we keep sampled writes async and limit retention to 7 days for the canary, the effort looks like 2–3 weeks of engineering + 1 week for QA/UI polish.

Action items I propose now:
- Soojin: spike the sampling + storage estimate (3d) — OBS-8912
- Jonas: implement the soft route cap toggle for Quasar (6–12h mitigation)
- Marissa: confirm Quasar’s willingness to enable extra logging for the 72h window and coordinate SE communication
- Avery: prioritize the fast-inspect spec in the next Console sprint planning and confirm acceptance criteria

Jonas
